terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the shop's site here after every move: it should print the same page and the same list every time.

tasks.title: Give the candles a file of their own
tasks.description:
Move the `catalogue` list from `src/shop.js` into `src/catalogue.js` and export it there with the name `catalogue`. In `shop.js`, import it in place of the list, so `node src/shop.js` prints the same page as before.

Check imports `catalogue.js` and compares the list with the one `shop.js` had. Then it puts other candles in a `catalogue.js` of its own and runs `shop.js`, to make sure the page comes from there.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on data in its own file.
Cut the list from `shop.js` and paste it into `catalogue.js`, with `export` in front of `const`.
At the top of `shop.js`, import `catalogue` from `catalogue.js`.
Run `node src/shop.js`: the page should look exactly as it did.
hints: A list can be exported like a function: an export line that names it, or `export` in front of the line that makes it.
`shop.js` still uses the name `catalogue` in its last lines. Once the list has moved, that name has to come from somewhere: an import line at the top.
`catalogue.js` holds `export const catalogue = [ ... ]`, and `shop.js` starts with `import { catalogue } from './catalogue.js'`.

tasks.title: Move the stock rules
tasks.description:
Move `isLow`, `inStock` and `lowStock` from `src/shop.js` into `src/stock.js`. Export `inStock` and `lowStock`; `isLow` only helps `lowStock`, so it is not exported. In `shop.js`, import what it still uses from `stock.js`. `shop.js` then imports from two files.

Check calls `inStock` and `lowStock` from `stock.js` with candles of its own, makes sure `shop.js` keeps no copy of them, and runs `shop.js` beside a `stock.js` of its own to make sure it uses that file.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on moving by what code is about and on one file importing from two.
Cut the three functions from `shop.js` and paste them into `stock.js`.
Export the two that other files need.
Run `node src/shop.js` and read the error it gives, if any: it names what `shop.js` is missing.
hints: After the move, run `shop.js`. A `ReferenceError` names a function that `shop.js` still uses but no longer has.
`shop.js` uses `lowStock` in its last line, and `productLine`, which is still in `shop.js` until Task 4, uses `inStock`. Both come from `stock.js` now.
`stock.js` has `export function inStock` and `export function lowStock`, with `isLow` above them without export. `shop.js` adds `import { inStock, lowStock } from './stock.js'`.

tasks.title: Read the low stock number from the settings
tasks.description:
`src/settings.js` came with the site, and it shares the shop's settings as its default export. In `src/stock.js`, import the settings from it, and make `isLow` use their `lowAt` in place of the `3` typed in. Leave `settings.js` as it is.

Check puts settings of its own in place of `settings.js`, with other numbers for `lowAt`, and calls `lowStock` from your `stock.js`. It also makes sure `settings.js` is unchanged.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on the default export, then read `settings.js`.
At the top of `stock.js`, import the settings, with a name of your choosing.
In `isLow`, use the `lowAt` of that object where the 3 is.
Run `node src/shop.js`: with `lowAt` at 3, the pour list is the same as before.
hints: `settings.js` has no names in curly braces to import. It shares one object, as its default export.
A default import has no curly braces, and the name after `import` is yours to choose. That name then holds the whole settings object.
`stock.js` starts with `import settings from './settings.js'`, and `isLow` compares with `settings.lowAt`.

tasks.title: Move the page into a file of its own
tasks.description:
Move `productLine` and `pageLines` from `src/shop.js` into `src/page.js`. `page.js` imports `inStock` from `stock.js` and the settings from `settings.js`, and `pageLines` starts the page with the settings' `shopName` in place of the name typed in. Export `pageLines`; `productLine` only helps it. In `shop.js`, import `pageLines`. After this task, `shop.js` keeps no function of its own: only its imports and the two lines that print.

Check calls `pageLines` from your `page.js` with settings and candles of its own, makes sure it uses `inStock` from `stock.js`, and runs `shop.js` beside a `page.js` of its own.
nextSteps: Cut the two functions from `shop.js` and paste them into `page.js`.
Give `page.js` its two imports: one from `stock.js`, one from `settings.js`.
Start the page with `shopName`, export `pageLines`, and import it in `shop.js`.
Remove from `shop.js` any import it no longer uses, and run it.
hints: Each file imports what it uses itself. `productLine` uses `inStock`, so `page.js` needs it from `stock.js`, whatever `shop.js` imports.
The settings come in the same way as in Task 3. Their `shopName` takes the place of the text at the start of the list `pageLines` gives.
`page.js` starts with `import { inStock } from './stock.js'` and `import settings from './settings.js'`; `pageLines` returns `[settings.shopName, ...candles.map(productLine)]`.
